summary.text: Son of Dardanus who died childless, so his brother Erichthonius succeeded to the kingdom in Apollodorus' account.
Not Ilus son of Tros who founded Ilium and fathered Laomedon — Apollodorus splits the name between this childless Dardanid and the later founder.

story.text: Dardanus had sons born to him, Ilus and Erichthonius, of whom Ilus died childless, and Erichthonius succeeded to the kingdom and married Astyoche, daughter of Simoeis, and begat Tros.
Homer compresses the line: Dardanus begat Erichthonius directly, with no intervening childless son; and the Ilus honored in the Iliad as founder with a barrow on the plain is elsewhere son of Tros.
